mechanism_narrative: A high level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its historical average compresses equity valuations by increasing discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 0.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 8.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE exceeds 8.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE is above 8.5% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over any 1-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a tightening monetary policy coinciding with labor market weakness, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 40% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE are rising, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, high residential construction (HOUST) and strong consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate robust economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances during late-cycle expansions when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month averages, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 in the last month signals an economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 95.0 in the last month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when INDPRO is below 95.0, or the Rank IC over any 1-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate strong demand conditions that support corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 40% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS are rising, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of total nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) relative to its historical average indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when PAYEMS is above its 5-year average, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 215.0 in the last month, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts monetary policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises above 215.0 in the last month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL is above 215.0, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.
